literal: Lin was at Shouyang and at odds with Mobile Court Director of the Secretariat Lu Qian; they slandered each other in turn. Summoned back to Ye, Wucheng was magnanimous and did not prosecute.
idiomatic: While Wang Lin held Shouyang he feuded with Lu Qian, director of the secretariat on the mobile court; they traded accusations until he was recalled to Ye. Emperor Wucheng let the matter pass without punishment.

literal: He was removed to be Inspector of Cangzhou; later Lin was made Grand Mentor and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: He was appointed inspector of Cangzhou, then made grand mentor and attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: The ridge of his dwelling for no reason split open; several sheng of red maggots came out, and where they fell to the ground turned to blood, writhing and moving.
idiomatic: The roof-ridge of his house split open for no reason. Several sheng of red maggots poured out; where they struck the ground they turned to blood and writhed.

literal: Again a dragon appeared in the ground outside the gate; cloud and mist rose, and the day grew dark.
idiomatic: A dragon also appeared in the ground outside his gate. Cloud and mist rose until broad daylight turned dim.

literal: When Chen general Wu Mingche came to invade, the emperor ordered Grand Guard General Yu Pohu and others out to relieve Qinzhou, and made Lin joint strategist.
idiomatic: When the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded, the emperor ordered Grand Guard General Yu Pohu and others to march out in relief toward Qinzhou and appointed Lin joint strategist.

literal: Lin said to those close: "Now Jupiter is in the southeast, the Year Star occupies the Ox-Northern Dipper zone, and Venus already rides high—all favor the guest. I shall meet death."
idiomatic: Lin told his intimates, "Jupiter stands in the southeast, the Year Star sits in the Ox and Dipper mansions, and Venus already rides high—all favor the attacker. I am marked for death."

literal: He also told Pohu: "Wu troops are very sharp; use a long strategy to master them—do not fight lightly."
idiomatic: He also told Yu Pohu, "Wu Mingche's men are keen. Wear them down with a long plan—do not join battle rashly."

literal: Pohu did not obey, joined battle, and the army was utterly defeated. Lin alone on horseback broke the encirclement and barely escaped.
idiomatic: Yu Pohu would not listen. He gave battle and the army was shattered. Lin broke out alone on horseback and barely lived.

literal: Returning to Pengcheng, the emperor ordered him at once to go to Shouyang and also permitted recruiting.
idiomatic: Back at Pengcheng the emperor ordered him straight to Shouyang and allowed him to raise troops.

literal: Lin was further advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Baling commandery.
idiomatic: Lin was further enfeoffed as prince of Baling commandery.

literal: Chen general Wu Mingche advanced to besiege him, dammed the Fei River to flood the city, while Pi Jinghe and others camped west of the Huai and in the end did not come to the rescue.
idiomatic: Wu Mingche pressed the siege, dammed the Fei to flood the city, while Pi Jinghe and others held west of the Huai—and never came to relieve it.

literal: Mingche attacked day and night; within the city damp and miasma spread, all suffered swelling, and the dead and sick lay piled together.
idiomatic: Mingche attacked without pause. Damp and foul air spread through the city; men swelled with sickness, and the dead and dying lay in heaps.

literal: From the seventh month to the tenth the city fell; he was taken captive, and the people wept as they followed him.
idiomatic: From the seventh month to the tenth the city fell. He was taken, and the people followed weeping.

literal: Wu Mingche, fearing he would stir trouble, killed him twenty li northeast of the city. He was forty-eight; the sound of weeping was like thunder.
idiomatic: Wu Mingche, fearing revolt, had him killed twenty li northeast of the city. He was forty-eight. The sound of mourning rolled like thunder.

literal: An old man came with wine and dried meat to pour libation, mourned to the full, gathered his blood, and went off with it in his bosom.
idiomatic: An old man brought wine and meat to pour a libation, mourned his fill, gathered the blood, and walked away with it hidden in his robe.

literal: The head was sent to Jiankang and hung in the market.
idiomatic: His head was sent to Jiankang and hung in the market.

literal: Lin's former clerk Zhu Yang, warehouse aide of the Liang Rapid-as-Wind Office, wrote to Chen Secretariat Director Xu Ling asking for Lin's head, saying:
idiomatic: Zhu Yang, a former clerk of Lin's in the Liang Rapid-as-Wind Office, wrote to Xu Ling, vice director of the Chen secretariat, begging for Lin's head. He said:

literal: I venture to think that as court and market shift and trade, the wind of bone-stub integrity is handed on; as dynasties turn, the track of loyal constancy is displayed.
idiomatic: I venture to say: as thrones and markets change hands, the stubborn bone of loyalty still passes down; as ages turn, the mark of steadfast service still shows.

literal: Thus when the House of Jin was near its end, Xu Guang was an old survivor of the Jin house;
idiomatic: When the Jin house was dying, Xu Guang remained its old loyal servant;

literal: when the Cao house had passed, Ma Fu was called a loyal minister of Wei.
idiomatic: when the Cao house had fallen, Ma Fu was hailed as Wei's faithful minister.

literal: By this they spread beauty in former books and left names to later ages.
idiomatic: So their praise entered the earlier histories and their names lived on.

literal: The late Liang Duke of Jianning, Lin, was a remnant scion of the Luoyang bank, an old clan of Yizhou; he achieved merit at the Dai commandery seat and service in the central court, and in the season of division bore the burden of a regional chief.
idiomatic: The late Liang Duke of Jianning, Lin, came of stock on the Luoyang shore and an old clan of Yizhou. He won merit at the Dai seat and served the central court; in an age of chaos he bore a governor's charge.

literal: Then he lightly gave his person to die for his lord and pledged his body to the state—truly following the track of past worthies, truly treading in the steps of former exemplars.
idiomatic: He gave his body cheaply to die for his lord and pledged his life to the state—truly in the footsteps of the worthies of old, truly walking the path of earlier men of honor.

literal: Yet Heaven tired of Liang virtue; above, he still thought to restore and continue—he only harbored the thought of Shen Baoxu, yet in the end met the calamity of Chang Hong.
idiomatic: Yet Heaven had turned from Liang; he still burned to restore the line—he kept Shen Baoxu's resolve, but met Chang Hong's fate.

literal: When the royal enterprise dawned bright and the tripod's mandate found its home, he then went far to the east of the mountains and entrusted his life to the north of the Yellow River.
idiomatic: When the royal cause brightened and the mandate found its throne, he withdrew to the lands east of the mountains and cast his lot north of the River.

literal: Though he sighed as a light-traveling subject, he still cherished the courtesy due a guest minister; moved by such a knowing friend, he forgot this gift of his person.
idiomatic: Though he grieved like a guest far from home, he was still treated as a valued ally; grateful for such trust, he thought nothing of giving his life.

literal: So that his body sank in the nine springs while his head traveled ten thousand li.
idiomatic: So his body went to the nine springs while his head traveled ten thousand li.

literal: Truly, to die wrapped in horse hide fulfilled the aim of his life;
idiomatic: To die wrapped in horsehide would have matched the wish of his life;

literal: to expose his bones on the wild plain would have met a minister's due.
idiomatic: to lie on the open field would still have been a subject's due.

literal: Yet body and head in different places—there is ground for grief;
idiomatic: Yet body and head in different places—there is cause enough for grief;

literal: no mound chosen, no trees planted—how deeply pitiable.
idiomatic: no grave mound marked, no trees planted—how deeply pitiable.

literal: Yang early took the lowest seat, humbled himself before Lord Xue's spit-and-grasp welcome, and bore Duke Wei's kindness in meeting him.
idiomatic: I early sat at the lowest place, humbled myself before Lord Xue's welcoming grasp, and bore Duke Wei's favor.

literal: For this my scarf is soaked and my sleeves rain—pain for a face I knew;
idiomatic: For this my scarf is drenched and my sleeves run with tears—for a face I knew;

literal: my bowels twist and my head aches—as if for a face still living.
idiomatic: my bowels twist and my head splits—as though he were still alive before me.

literal: I bow and think how your sacred grace is broad and deep; your bright edict has gone forth, pardoning Wang Jing's weeping and granting Tian Heng's burial. Though Yang is grass-low and mean, in secret I too have a heart.
idiomatic: I bow before your broad grace: your edict has gone forth to spare Wang Jing's mourners and grant Tian Heng his burial. Though I am mean as grass, I too have a heart.

literal: Lin once governed Shouyang and left much lingering kindness;
idiomatic: Lin once held Shouyang and left kindness behind;

literal: he once traveled the lands right of the river—not without remaining virtue.
idiomatic: he once served south of the Yangtze—not without merit left.

literal: Shoulder to shoulder with clerks of the Eastern Pavilion, following in the steps of guests of the Western Garden—we ask to return him to that country and restore his tomb.
idiomatic: Men of the Eastern Pavilion stood at his side; guests of the Western Garden followed in his train—we beg to bring him back to that land and raise his grave.

literal: If only the lonely mound is built, perhaps swallows will fly carrying earth;
idiomatic: If his lonely mound is raised, perhaps swallows will come bearing soil;

literal: a rich stele set up in due form, and from time to time those who shed tears will remain.
idiomatic: a noble stele set up, and men who weep will linger there.

literal: Recently old associates Wang Wan and others already submitted a memorial; we looked up to receive the court's deliberation, but our plea was not granted.
idiomatic: Lately Wang Wan and other old companions already filed a petition; we awaited the court's ruling, but our request was denied.

literal: In former days when Duke Lian passed, a grave domain was built at once on the Fei River;
idiomatic: When Duke Lian died of old, a tomb was raised straightway on the Fei;

literal: when Sun Shu passed, catalpa and oak were planted still at Shaobo.
idiomatic: when Sun Shu died, catalpa and oak were planted still at Shaobo.

literal: From this speaking, there is indeed precedent to restrain us.
idiomatic: By these examples, precedent plainly stands.

literal: Let it not be that below the walls of Shouchun there pass only men who bring word of Ge;
idiomatic: Do not leave below Shouchun's walls only the cold bearer of ill tidings;

literal: on the isle of Cangzhou, only the guest who grieves for Tian.
idiomatic: on some bleak isle, only Tian Heng's lone mourner.

literal: Risking death I state this prayer; I bow and await punishment.
idiomatic: At the risk of my life I make this plea; I bow and await your judgment.

literal: Ling praised his purpose and constancy.
idiomatic: Xu Ling praised his loyalty and resolve.

literal: Mingche too repeatedly dreamed that Lin begged for his head; both reported to the Chen ruler, who granted it.
idiomatic: Wu Mingche too dreamed again and again that Lin begged for his head. Both men reported to the Chen ruler, who consented.

literal: Then with Opening Office, Equal in Insignia chief clerk Liu Shaohui and others they carried the head back to the Huai south and provisionally buried it on the flank of Eight Lords Mountain; sworn followers who came to the funeral numbered several thousand.
idiomatic: Then Liu Shaohui, chief clerk with opening office and equal insignia, and others carried the head back to the south Huai and buried it provisionally on the slope of Eight Lords Mountain. Several thousand old followers came to the grave.

literal: Yang and the others then by hidden paths returned north and separately arranged to receive the remains.
idiomatic: Zhu Yang and his party then stole north by back roads and made separate plans to bring the body home.

literal: Before long five men of Yangzhou, Mao Zhisheng and others, secretly sent the coffin through and delivered it at Ye.
idiomatic: Soon five Yangzhou men, Mao Zhisheng among them, secretly conveyed the coffin through and delivered it at Ye.

literal: Posthumously he was given Commander-in-Chief of fifteen provinces, Inspector of Yangzhou, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Mentor, Opening Office, and Recorder of the Secretariat Affairs; his posthumous title was Loyal Martial King, and a funerary carriage with covered canopy was granted for the burial.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made commander-in-chief over fifteen provinces, inspector of Yangzhou, attendant-in-ordinary, grand mentor, with opening office and recorder of the secretariat; his temple name was Loyal Martial King, and a state funerary carriage was granted.

literal: Lin's bearing was easy and refined; his hair when he stood trailed to the ground; joy and anger did not show on his face.
idiomatic: Lin's bearing was calm and elegant. Standing, his hair reached the ground; joy and anger never showed on his face.

literal: Though he had no learning, he was strong in memory and inwardly keen; the aides and clerks of his army and headquarters numbered in the thousands, and he knew all their names.
idiomatic: He had no schooling, but his memory was fierce and his mind quick; a thousand officers and clerks served him, and he knew every name.

literal: Punishment he did not abuse; he was light with wealth and loved his officers, and won the hearts of commanders and soldiers.
idiomatic: He did not abuse punishment; he was free with goods and cherished his men, and won soldiers and officers alike.

literal: From youth he bore command; he passed through many ruinous times and by nature had the constancy of loyalty and righteousness.
idiomatic: From youth he held command, lived through repeated collapses, and by nature kept the knot of loyalty.

literal: Though his original design was not fulfilled, the people of Ye for this also held him in esteem and treated him very generously.
idiomatic: Though his great design failed, the men of Ye respected him for it and treated him generously.

literal: When he was defeated and taken by Chen troops, Wu Mingche wished to spare him, but the generals under him were mostly Lin's former clerks; they vied to plead for him and all supplied him—Mingche for this grew jealous, feared he would stir trouble, and so he met disaster.
idiomatic: After his defeat the Chen army took him. Wu Mingche meant to spare him, but many of his own officers had once served Lin; they crowded forward to plead for him and gave him supplies. Mingche grew jealous, feared trouble, and so brought him to his death.

literal: At the time, farmers and rustics, whether they knew him or not, none did not sigh and weep for him.
idiomatic: Then field hands and villagers, whether they had known him or not, all sighed and wept.

literal: Seeing how his sincerity and faith moved things—even General Li's gentle, persuasive manner can scarcely add to this.
idiomatic: To see how his honesty moved men—even General Li Guang's gentle way with troops could hardly match it.

literal: Lin had seventeen sons.
idiomatic: Lin had seventeen sons.

literal: The eldest son Jing inherited the princely title in Qi; at the end of Wuping he was Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate.
idiomatic: The eldest, Jing, inherited the princedom in Qi; at the end of Wuping he was regular attendant of the palace gate.

literal: The ninth son Yan, in Sui's Kaihuang era was Opening Office, Equal in Insignia with Three Departments; at the start of Daye he died as Inspector of Yuzhou.
idiomatic: The ninth son, Yan, under Sui Kaihuang held opening office, equal in insignia with three departments; early in Daye he died as inspector of Yuzhou.

literal: Footnote 1 in the source text.
idiomatic: Footnote 1 in the source text.

literal: The complete text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
